#!/bin/bash
# Ashenvale Idle - Pterodactyl install script
# Runs in a temporary container; the server files live in /mnt/server
set -e
apt-get update -qq
apt-get install -y -qq git ca-certificates > /dev/null

mkdir -p /mnt/server
cd /mnt/server

GIT_ADDRESS="${GIT_ADDRESS:-https://github.com/IhleMa/ashenvale-idle}"
BRANCH="${BRANCH:-main}"
[[ "${GIT_ADDRESS}" != *.git ]] && GIT_ADDRESS="${GIT_ADDRESS}.git"

# Private repositories: use a GitHub username + personal access token
if [[ -n "${USERNAME}" && -n "${ACCESS_TOKEN}" ]]; then
  GIT_ADDRESS="https://${USERNAME}:${ACCESS_TOKEN}@$(echo -e "${GIT_ADDRESS}" | cut -d/ -f3-)"
fi

if [[ -d .git ]]; then
  echo "Existing installation found - updating"
  git remote set-url origin "${GIT_ADDRESS}"
  git fetch origin "${BRANCH}"
  git reset --hard "origin/${BRANCH}"
elif [[ -n "$(ls -A /mnt/server 2>/dev/null)" ]]; then
  echo "Folder not empty - cloning into a temp folder and copying (player data in ./data is kept)"
  rm -rf /tmp/ashenvale
  git clone --branch "${BRANCH}" --single-branch "${GIT_ADDRESS}" /tmp/ashenvale
  cp -a /tmp/ashenvale/. /mnt/server/
else
  git clone --branch "${BRANCH}" --single-branch "${GIT_ADDRESS}" .
fi

npm install --omit=dev --no-audit --no-fund --no-save
mkdir -p data public/assets
echo "-----------------------------------------"
echo " Ashenvale Idle installed successfully!"
echo "-----------------------------------------"

variables.name: Git Repository
variables.description: GitHub repository to install the game from.

variables.name: Branch
variables.description: Git branch to install and update from.

variables.name: Auto Update
variables.description: Pull the latest code from GitHub on every start (1 = yes, 0 = no).

variables.name: Git Username
variables.description: Only needed if the repository is PRIVATE: your GitHub username.

variables.name: Git Access Token
variables.description: Only needed if the repository is PRIVATE: a GitHub personal access token with read access to the repo.

variables.name: Allow Registration
variables.description: Allow new players to create accounts on first start (true/false). Afterwards this can be toggled live on the Admin page.

variables.name: Trust Proxy
variables.description: Set to true only if the game runs behind a reverse proxy (nginx, Cloudflare) so login rate-limiting sees real player IPs.

variables.name: Admin Users
variables.description: Comma-separated usernames that get access to the in-game Admin page (e.g. alice,bob). You can also use the console command: admin add <username>

variables.name: HTTPS Mode
variables.description: off = plain HTTP (default). auto = free Let's Encrypt certificate, obtained and renewed automatically (needs Domain; with Cloudflare DNS also the Cloudflare API Token). files = use your own certificate files (TLS Certificate / TLS Key). Players then open https://your-domain:PORT; http:// on the same port redirects automatically.

variables.name: Domain
variables.description: Domain (or subdomain) whose DNS A record points at this server's IP, e.g. game.example.com. Several names: comma separated. Needed for HTTPS Mode auto.

variables.name: Let's Encrypt E-Mail
variables.description: Optional e-mail for Let's Encrypt (warnings if a certificate is about to expire without being renewed).

variables.name: Certificate Check
variables.description: How Let's Encrypt checks that you own the domain. dns-cloudflare (recommended): a temporary DNS record via the Cloudflare API — works on any port. http: needs a second allocation that is reachable from the internet as port 80, set as HTTP Redirect Port.

variables.name: Cloudflare API Token
variables.description: For Certificate Check dns-cloudflare: a Cloudflare API token with permission Zone → DNS → Edit for your domain (Cloudflare → My Profile → API Tokens → Create Token → template "Edit zone DNS").

variables.name: Let's Encrypt Staging
variables.description: 1 = use Let's Encrypt's test environment (certificates browsers do NOT trust, but no rate limits) to try the setup. Set back to 0 when it works — the real certificate is then fetched automatically.

variables.name: TLS Certificate
variables.description: For HTTPS Mode files: certificate chain (PEM), relative to the server folder.

variables.name: TLS Key
variables.description: For HTTPS Mode files: private key (PEM), relative to the server folder.

variables.name: HTTP Redirect Port
variables.description: Optional: a second allocation (ideally reachable as port 80) that redirects http:// to https:// and answers the Let's Encrypt http check. Leave empty if not needed — the game port already redirects http:// itself.
